capabilities.request: Read the whole thread, a Slack message someone links, or an image someone posted, before answering

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Nothing beyond setup
capabilities.result: An answer that takes in the whole thread and any message or image it links to
capabilities.limit: Reads as you, through your Slack tab. The clone posts only through Misha, never with a Slack tool of its own.

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: A folder linked on Settings
capabilities.result: A marked answer naming the files it read
capabilities.limit: Reads your linked folders as they are on this Mac, uncommitted work included, which may not be what is merged. One bounded read; tracing behaviour across the code is research.

capabilities.request: Say who changed something, when and why, from the commits

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: A folder linked on Settings
capabilities.result: Who changed it, when and why, naming each commit by its short hash
capabilities.limit: By default the history of the branch each folder has checked out, and a remote's branches only as you last fetched them. A pull request's discussion is not in it.

capabilities.request: Read Jira tickets and Confluence pages

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Jira and Confluence on Set up
capabilities.result: An answer naming the ticket or page it read
capabilities.limit: Whoever the clone answers may get what it read.

capabilities.request: Create, edit, comment on, link or move Jira tickets and Confluence pages

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Jira and Confluence on Set up
capabilities.result: The change, and a reply saying what changed
capabilities.limit: Only what your own messages in that turn ask for. Someone you allow to ask for work does not get these tools.

capabilities.request: Read Google Docs and Sheets, comments included

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Google Workspace on Set up
capabilities.result: An answer naming the Doc or Sheet it read
capabilities.limit: Whoever the clone answers may get what it read.

capabilities.request: Create a Doc from text, edit a Doc, write to a Sheet, or comment on either

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Google Workspace on Set up
capabilities.result: The change, and a reply saying what changed
capabilities.limit: Only what your own messages in that turn ask for.

capabilities.request: Find a meeting's transcript and answer from it

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Fireflies on Set up
capabilities.result: An answer naming the meeting it read
capabilities.limit: Reads transcripts Fireflies already has. It does not join or record meetings.

capabilities.request: Find a Figma screen, read its text and specs, or render it as an image in the reply

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: Figma on Set up
capabilities.result: The screen's text and specs, or its image attached to the reply
capabilities.limit: Reads and renders only. It cannot change a design.

capabilities.request: Run GitHub CLI commands, such as reading a pull request's checks

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: The GitHub CLI signed in, which Set up checks
capabilities.result: What the command showed, or what it changed
capabilities.limit: One command at a time, as your GitHub account. Never a staging or production deployment or a release.

capabilities.request: Run AWS CLI commands in a session for the environments a question needs, such as reading logs

routes.surface: in its own turn, answering in Slack

needs: AWS on Set up
capabilities.result: What the commands showed, or what they changed
capabilities.limit: One command at a time, as your AWS access. Never a staging or production deployment or a release.

capabilities.request: Investigate a question a quick read can't answer, and report with sources

routes.surface: started by the clone, which reports in Slack

needs: For a question about code, a folder linked on Settings
For an incident, read access to that environment's logs and data
capabilities.result: An answer from the worker's report, with its sources and what stays uncertain
capabilities.limit: Read-only because its brief says so, not because the system prevents writes. It reports what stays uncertain.

capabilities.request: Make a change in your code, in a worktree of its own, up to a pull request

routes.surface: started by the clone, which reports in Slack

needs: A folder linked on Settings, with the remote its pull requests go to
capabilities.result: A pull request on the remote, merged only where workers may merge
capabilities.limit: How far it goes is the request's and your routines' call, within Settings. Staging, production and releases stay yours, and a change in someone else's repository needs their approval in their own message.

capabilities.request: Do work that needs no repository, such as summarising a meeting or researching a ticket

routes.surface: started by the clone, which reports in Slack

needs: The connectors the work reads, on Set up
capabilities.result: What the worker found or made, reported in the thread
capabilities.limit: Runs in a scratch folder of its own. A routine can say how such work is done, and grants no access.

capabilities.request: List, open and read your signed-in browser tabs as compact outlines, wait for a page, screenshot a tab, or list the requests it sent

routes.surface: through the misha-browser MCP server
through Misha's MCP server in your own Claude Code and OpenCode, while Browser control is on

needs: The misha-browser MCP server registered in your agent, or Browser control on, on Set up
The Misha Browser extension and native host in Chrome or Brave
capabilities.result: Page outlines, screenshots and request lists in the agent's session
capabilities.limit: Acts through your signed-in sessions on any site the browser has open. The extension records every tab's requests while it runs, with credentials redacted by name and pattern. Misha gives none of these tools to the clone or its workers.

capabilities.request: Click, drag, type, fill forms, press keys and scroll in a tab with real input

routes.surface: through the misha-browser MCP server
through Misha's MCP server in your own Claude Code and OpenCode, while Browser control is on

needs: The misha-browser MCP server registered in your agent, or Browser control on, on Set up
The Misha Browser extension and native host in Chrome or Brave
Accessibility and Screen Recording for the app that runs your agent
capabilities.result: The input made, and what changed on the page
capabilities.limit: The input is a real mouse and keyboard on your Mac, so it acts wherever the pointer and focus are. Misha gives none of these tools to the clone or its workers.

capabilities.request: Move the Mac's mouse, type and press keys, capture the screen, list apps and bring one to the front

routes.surface: through the misha-browser MCP server
through Misha's MCP server in your own Claude Code and OpenCode, while Browser control is on

needs: The misha-browser MCP server registered in your agent, or Browser control on, on Set up
Accessibility and Screen Recording for the app that runs your agent, except to list and focus apps
capabilities.result: The input made, a screen capture, or the list of apps
capabilities.limit: macOS only. A screen capture shows whatever is on screen. Misha gives none of these tools to the clone or its workers.
